chapter: After high school: riverfront and tailoring
title: Rampart Street as the Black main street and its tailor shops
summary: He describes Rampart, Dryades and Dryad Streets as the Black business area, the tailor shops, suit prices then and now, and shopping in Dallas.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: So, what was, when you talked about Rampart Street, was that like the happening?

Rampart Street was anywhere between the 1930s and the 50s. Rampart Street was the happening place. You got to remember that every major city before the development of the shopping malls and the shopping centers had its main street like Canal Street was the main street basically for white folks at that particular. Rampart Street and Dryad Street and for Red Street was the streets in New Orleans were basically for black people. And the people who had industries and businesses in Washington Avenue, Rampart Street, Dryad Street, at one time Rampart Street had somewhere like around about 15 or 20 Taylor Shops. Because that's when everybody wanted to have their clothes made. Because the old standard, see when I was a kid, before I had long pants I had the knickers that came up the leg, you see. And hell, I wanted long pants like everybody else. I just didn't want any knickers. So, that's how it all happened. And, you know, with the zoot suit, the long coat, with the big wide knee and tight.
